synchronousDesignConstraints: StableValueStorage.write and ProductGenerationStorage.replace return void; ProductGenerationBackend.withExclusiveWrite<T>(operation: () => T): T is explicitly synchronous.

Userscript and Tauri withExclusiveWrite release their writing flag in finally when the callback returns. Returning a Promise would release protection before staged validation/publication; merely inserting awaits is invalid.

Runtime adapters synchronously update in-memory/current mirror state and queue durable GM/IPC writes. Tauri serializes the complete staged ProductSnapshot to localStorage per raw write. This benchmark excludes that native-mirror cost.

A real nonblocking design needs an explicit async commit/preparation contract, detached bounded candidates, serialized runtime writer ownership, session/revision checks after each yield and before pointer publication, flush/disposal/error semantics, and crash/interleaving tests in both runtimes. This is broader than the isolated checksum change and remains an open C00 task.
